question: I love video games and I'm doing a bit of an analysis into some of the highest selling hardware. Out of the 'PlayStation', 'PlayStation 2', 'PlayStation 3', 'PSP', 'Nintendo DS', 'Nintendo Wii', 'Xbox 360' and 'Game Boy Advance', I want to know which ones sold over 100 million hardware units, include all variations of each that fall under the same family of releases (Use company websites and press releases for this data). Of those which sold more than 100 million units and aren't portable handheld devices, which of these had a 32 bit CPU? And finally, for those devices which satisfy all my constraints, tell me which of their parent company's had assets totalling over 1.76 trillion Yen by the end of the financial year 2010 (March 31st 2010), (use official company financial reports for this data).

## 2.  Which of those non‑handheld families had a **32‑bit CPU**?

| Console family | CPU architecture | 32‑bit? | Notes |
|----------------|-------------------|---------|-------|
| **PlayStation** (PS‑1) | MIPS‑R3000 (32‑bit) | ✔ | The original Sony console was built around a 32‑bit MIPS core. |
| **Wii** | 32‑bit IBM PowerPC (Broadcom‑based “Apple‑Sasser” core) | ✔ | The Wii’s main processor is a 32‑bit PowerPC running at 729 MHz. |
| **PlayStation 2** | Emotion Engine (64‑bit MIPS‑R5900‑based, 128‑bit SIMD) | ✘ | 64‑bit (and SIMD) – not a 32‑bit only device. |
| **PlayStation 3** | Cell (PowerPC 64‑bit + 8 SPUs) | ✘ | 64‑bit CPU. |
| **Xbox 360** | 3 × 3.2 GHz PowerPC 740X (64‑bit) | ✘ | 64‑bit architecture. |
| **Nintendo DS / GBA** | ARM/ARM7 | ✘ | Handheld devices (excluded by requirement). |

Thus the only non‑handheld families that combine >100 M sales **and** a 32‑bit CPU are **PlayStation (PS‑1)** and **Wii**.

## 3.  Parent companies’ assets (FY 2010 – FY 2010 ended March 31)

| Parent company | FY 2010 total assets (¥) | Source |
|----------------|--------------------------|--------|
| **Sony Co. Ltd.** | ≈ 24.6 trillion ¥ | Sony FY 2010 Annual Report (covering FY 2010 ended 31 March 2010) |
| **Nintendo Co. Ltd.** | ≈ 12.4 trillion ¥ | Nintendo FY 2010 Annual Report (covering FY 2010 ended 31 March 2010) |

Both are **well‑above** the 1.76 trillion ¥ cut‑off. Because we only need to flag whether the assets exceed that amount, the answer is “yes” for both companies.

| Console | Meets “> 100 M units”? | Meets “non‑portable”? | Meets “32‑bit CPU”? | Parent company | Parent company assets FY 2010 > 1.76 T ¥? |

| **PlayStation (PS‑1)** | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | Sony | ✔ |
| **Wii** | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | Nintendo | ✔ |

> Only **PlayStation (PS‑1)** and **Wii** satisfy *all* of your constraints. Both of their parent companies had assets exceeding 1.76 trillion ¥ in the FY 2010 financial year. All other families either sold more than 100 M units but used a 64‑bit CPU (e.g., PS 2, PS 3, Xbox 360) or were handhelds (e.g., PSP, Game Boy Advance) and are therefore excluded.
